Narrative Eligibility Justification Provide a detailed explanation of the resource’s eligibility for the National Register, including supporting historic information, methods for evaluation under the four criteria, discussion of the seven aspects of integrity, and conclusions about eligibility. Building 06-CP-65, referred to as the Technical Support Building, has been determined to be a contributing element to the Area 6 Control Point Historic District (O’Neill et al. 2021; Reed 2022). It contributes to the significance of the historic district under Criterion A as one of the principal buildings that supported timing and firing operations for nuclear testing on the NNSS from 1966 to 1992. As such, the building served as a major warehouse with office and laboratory space within the district. It was used by Reynolds Electrical and Engineering Company (REECo), a long-time general contractor that provided extensive support for many day-to-day site operations for the Control Point and throughout the NNSS. It was also used by Edgerton, Germeshausen, and Grier, Inc (EG&G), which provided direct technical support to the national laboratories and the Department of Defense (DOD). Beginning in the 1970s, it was an important staging area and electrical power supply point for the NNSS diagnostic trailer fleet. Its unique location immediately along Mercury Highway in Yucca Pass allowed easy accessibility to the forward area of the NNSS. The building also contributes to the historic Nevada SHPO – ARA Form Page 1 SHPO Resource #: B18910 Rev. 2017 Other Resource #: 06-CP-65 district under Criterion C as it is one of the large, unadorned, precast concrete buildings at the Control Point. These types of buildings were the prominent architectural elements of the compound that conveyed the district’s overall utilitarian, military-industrial character. Building 06-CP-65 retains all aspects of integrity to a high degree and easily conveys its significance as a warehouse that supported Control Point operations. Between 1966, when it was built, to the end of the nuclear testing period in 1992, the building’s office space was primarily outfitted for engineers, certain administrative functions, and as laboratories.
